clue.text: People go on, mostly quiet and unknown

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to go on is to happen or take place
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: People carry on chatting, mostly in hushed tones, about something nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb, as in to people a land with settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a place is to fill it with inhabitants, which is to take up residence there and occupy it.

clue.text: Abandoned rest, unprepared

blocks.note: a match called off is abandoned
the balance is the remainder or rest

explanation.surface: Someone gave up resting and was caught unready.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught off balance means taken by surprise and not ready to react, so unprepared.

clue.text: A tribute for each working person adhering to routine

indicators.note: working suggests letters set in motion and reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A tribute paid to every employee who sticks to a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone who always follows the same fixed patterns and dislikes change.

clue.text: Look closely, apprehending weight in alloy

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing hold of, so one word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: to peer is to look searchingly
wt is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Inspecting closely while catching a heavy metal object.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a grey alloy chiefly of tin, traditionally with lead, used for tankards and plates.

clue.text: Unfair skill is possessed by Greek god

indicators.note: something possessed is held by its owner, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild and shepherds
an art is a craft or skill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that some divine talent gives a Greek deity an unfair advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan view is biased towards one side, and so not fair or impartial.

clue.text: Grant, humble, supporting Pacino?

indicators.note: in a down clue a word supporting another sits beneath it, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: Al Pacino is the American film actor
low means lowly or humble

explanation.surface: A modest actor in a supporting role to Al Pacino.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts a word underneath, so the humble word goes below the actor's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a request is to permit it, which is to allow it.

clue.text: Indiscreet stories about court and head of state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stories wrap round the court
head of points to the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: tales are stories
ct is the abbreviation for court
the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Gossip about the royal court and the head of state that shows no discretion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tactless lacks diplomacy and says things without thinking of others' feelings, so is indiscreet.

clue.text: Grotesque mask, one with depth, reflects deception

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted out of natural shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter
taken as written
d is the abbreviation for depth
mirrors reflect, so to reflect is to mirror

explanation.surface: A hideous mask with real depth reveals a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply joins depth to the other fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from conjurors' tricks, means illusion and trickery designed to obscure the truth.

clue.text: Crazy shock coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to stun is to shock or stupefy

explanation.surface: A wild surprise on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal slang for mad, as in going nuts.

clue.text: Moderate when in command

indicators.note: in places the word for when inside the word for command

blocks.note: a decree is an order
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone tempers their behaviour once they are in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to lessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to reduce or tone it down, which is to decrease it.

clue.text: Not detained, turn for coast

blocks.note: someone not detained is free
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: Released from custody, someone heads for the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' reads as the seashore, but it is the verb: to move along without power.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to ride a bicycle or drive without pedalling or engine power, which is exactly to coast.

clue.text: Cold, ill-mannered man in power

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lout is a rude, uncouth man

explanation.surface: A frosty, boorish man holding office.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for influence or political weight, the ability to get things done.

clue.text: Directly demolished cheat's argument following fabrications

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter
a row is a quarrel
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
fabrications are untruths

explanation.surface: A cheat's case is demolished once his lies are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: f. is the standard abbreviation for 'following', as in pp. 10f.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a straight line, the shortest route between two points, so going there directly.

clue.text: Step round plant and large insect

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the step encloses the plant

blocks.note: a stage is a step in a process
beet is a root vegetable plant
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Walking around a plant to find a big bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The stag beetle is a large European beetle whose male has antler-like jaws.

clue.text: Delicate and risky, ignoring hospital

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: hairy is informal for dangerous or frightening
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A fragile, dangerous procedure that bypasses the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy describes something light and insubstantial, as in airy lace, so fine and delicate.

clue.text: Crass act on ground regarded as holy

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken down, so the preceding letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A crude stunt performed on hallowed ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like it belongs with ground, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means sacred and inviolable, too important or holy to be interfered with.

clue.text: Revolutionary, about to honour rising, started again

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the words are read upwards, from end to start
about means surrounding, so the revolutionary wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
taken as written
the OBE is the British honour Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A revolutionary, about to be honoured, rose again.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To reboot a computer is to start it up again, and by extension to restart anything.

clue.text: Clan again badly missing a church member

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named letter is taken out
badly means done wrong, so the remaining letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken letter by letter
the article taken as the letter

explanation.surface: A family once more poorly served by an absent churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican belongs to the Church of England or a related church in the worldwide Anglican Communion.

clue.text: Porcelain produced back in top year

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end to its start
in places the turned word inside the other words

blocks.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hill
animals produced by a breeder are bred
y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Fine china brought out again during its best year.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown Derby is a long-established English porcelain maker from the city of Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a famous brand of English bone china, so the name stands for the porcelain itself.

clue.text: Fool after end of exams becoming complacent

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word only

blocks.note: the word's closing letter
a mug is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: An idiot gets cocky once the exams are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the fool after the letter, though the fool comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes being self-satisfied and pleased with oneself, which is to be complacent.

clue.text: Wreck? It may be on the rocks

definitions.text: It may be on the rocks

blocks.note: first meaning: to thwart or put an end to a plan

blocks.clueFragment: It may be on the rocks
blocks.note: second meaning: a whisky that may be served over ice

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' and 'wreck' suggest a ship run aground; in a bar the phrase means served with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to put an end to it, and the whisky from Scotland is often drunk with ice.

clue.text: Scare superstar with worry about new spicy dish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for worry wraps round a letter

blocks.note: to chill is to frighten, as in a chilling tale
an icon is a celebrated figure
care is anxiety or concern
n is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A celebrity is frightened by a new hot dish they're worried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scare' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning frighten, giving chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a hot stew of minced beef, beans and chilli peppers, a famously spicy dish.

clue.text: Bar outclassing others to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so a stretch of the following words is used

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A pub that partly outclasses its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, especially gold or silver, usually shaped as a bar.

clue.text: Help to keep leader in contest sharp

indicators.note: leader in points to the first letter of the next word
to keep means to hold inside, so the help word encloses a letter

blocks.note: aid is help
the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Assistance to keep the front-runner ahead in a tight race.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective describes a sour or biting taste or remark, so sharp.

clue.text: Novice in charge of measurement of volume

blocks.note: a cub is a beginner, as in cub reporter
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A newcomer is put in charge of measuring capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival in sense: a cubic measure is one of volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes three-dimensional units such as cubic metres, used to measure volume.

clue.text: Heavy garment in crate awkwardly carried by kid?

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so the letters are jumbled
carried by means held inside, so the jumbled letters go within the next word

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter
a kid is a young goat; the question mark flags the loose fit

explanation.surface: A child struggles to carry a bulky coat packed in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' suggests a child, but it is a young goat, which is then loosely used for the goat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a long, thick overcoat, especially one worn by soldiers, so a heavy garment.

clue.text: Set off from school in time

indicators.note: in places the school inside the word for time

blocks.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving school on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or charge is to make it explode, which is to detonate it.

clue.text: Not indecent, hurried in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, not read

blocks.note: chased means hurried after someone

explanation.surface: Someone who talks quickly but keeps it clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, free of anything lewd, so not indecent.
